key_insight: LangDiT shows that transformer architecture choices materially improve continuous diffusion language models, not just the diffusion objective or sampler.
engineering_relevance: For CDLM deployment, the paper suggests architecture-level tuning can deliver better generation quality at the same training objective and inference pipeline.
method: Systematically compared transformer designs for CDLMs rather than reusing causal LLM or DiT backbones.
Added feature and query-key normalization, wider noise conditioning, likelihood-shortcut gradient routing/calibration, and confidence-gated self-conditioning.
Used LangDiT as a plug-and-play backbone across LangFlow and Plaid-style CDLM formulations.
evidence_signal: On OpenWebText unconditional 1024-token generation, LangDiT reached 21.72 GenPPL at 1024 NFEs and 44.72 at 128 NFEs with LangFlow, and 11.33/27.51 GenPPL in Plaid-style CDLMs.
watch_item: Reported gains depend on specific CDLM formulations and NFE budgets, so the added architectural complexity may need careful re-tuning to reproduce in other setups.
paper_title: Designing Transformers for Continuous Diffusion Language Models
